062/**
063 * Database specific operations and access mechanisms.
064 * An implementation manages and uses a {@code sharedConnection},
065 * See {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.SsUtils#dbSupport()} for best access method.
066 */
067// This needs work, clean up. It evolved as someplace to put stuff that
068// shouldn't be in mainline code; and it provides a way to find out where those
069// places are.
070// TODO: Get rid of the RowSet param since only one database.
071//       But then getConnection still needs way to determine DataSource or URL.
072public interface DbSupport {
073  /**
074   * Return an open connection for quick use that
075   * connects to the database where the row set comes from.
076   * <em>Do not close</em> the returned connection after use.
077   * Using this to create a ResultSet/JdbcRowSet that stays open
078   * is <em>not quick</em>.
079   *
080   * @return connection, may be null
081   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
082   */
083  Connection getSharedConnection() throws SQLException;
084
085  // NOT USED
086  // /**
087  //  * Return a connection to the {@code RowSet}'s database using information
088  //  * from the {@code RowSet} to get the connection; <em>close when finished</em>.
089  //  * Tries {@code RowSet}'s DataSource then url.
090  //  * @param rs row set from target database
091  //  * @return connection
092  //  * @throws java.sql.SQLException
093  //  */
094  // Connection getConnection(RowSet rs) throws SQLException;
095
096  /**
097   * Create a query that contains the row number of a non "order by" query.
098   * When used in conjunction with a {@link SsDbComboBox2} which is acting as
099   * a combobox navigator, the row number is used to avoid sequential searches
100   * table searches in {@link dev.visdb.seesaw.utils.SyncManager}.
101   * For example, given {@snippet lang="java":
102   * sup.createRownumQuery("part_id, part_name",
103   *                       "rown",
104   *                       "part_data",
105   *                       "ORDER BY part_name");
106   * }
107   * The {@code H2} {@code DbSupport} uses the the {@code H2} builtin
108   * function {@code ROWNUM()}
109   * and returns the string {@snippet :
110   * SELECT part_id, part_name, ROWNUM() AS rown
111   * FROM part_data
112   * ORDER BY part_name;
113   * }
114   * <p>
115   * Note that Mariadb has ROWNUM() and Oracle has ROWNUM; they perform
116   * a similar function. Other databases use ROW_NUMBER() in more complex
117   * windowed queries, example fragment of a more complex query: {@snippet :
118   * ROW_NUMBER() OVER(ORDER BY (SELECT NULL))
119   * }
120   * refer to your database documentation, or AI assistant, for implementing
121   * this method.
122   *
123   * @param selectColumns could be "*"
124   * @param rownumberColumn
125   * @param tableName
126   * @param trailingClause for example "ORDER BY someCol"
127   * @return query or null
128   */
129  // Mariadb: ROWNUM(), oracle has ROWNUM.
130  default String createRownumQuery(String selectColumns, String rownumberColumn, String tableName,
131                                   String trailingClause) {
132    return null;
133  }
134
135  /**
136   * Examine the specified JDBCType.ARRAY's columns metadata,
137   * and return the array's element type.
138   * See {@link H2DbSupport} for a database specific
139   * example that should also work with HSQLDB and DuckDB.
140   * Best to provide a DB specific implementation.
141   * <p>
142   * This default implementation is based on Google search AI. The AI claims
143   * this works with PostgreSQL, H2, HSQLDB, ClickHouse, MySQL/TiDB, Oracle,
144   * DuckDB, and SQL Server.
145   *
146   * @param rmd
147   * @param columnIndex
148   * @return
149   * @throws SQLException
150   */
151  default JDBCType resolveArrayElementType(ResultSetMetaData rmd, int columnIndex)
152      throws SQLException {
153    JDBCType columnType = JDBCType.valueOf(rmd.getColumnType(columnIndex));
154    if (columnType != JDBCType.ARRAY)
155      throw new IllegalArgumentException("Column must be JDBCType.ARRAY, not " + columnType);
156
157    String typeName = getVendorTypeNameForArray(rmd, columnIndex);
158
159    // Lookup metadata type identifier in cross-vendor dictionary mapping
160    JDBCType standardType = vendorTypeMap().get(typeName);
161    if (standardType != null) {
162      return standardType;
163    }
164
165    // Fallback strategy:
166    // Try to directly instantiate from matching standard JDBCType enum value name.
167    try {
168      return JDBCType.valueOf(typeName); // Seems hopeless
169    } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
170      // Unresolved dialect or complex user-defined structural type (UDT)
171      throw new IllegalArgumentException(JStuff.sf("'%s' is not a JDBCType", typeName));
172    }
173  }
174
175  /**
176   * Run the function using the shared connection, return the result.
177   * @param <R>
178   * @param func
179   * @return
180   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
181   */
182  default<R> R runWithConnection(FunctionSQL<Connection, R> func) throws SQLException {
183    return func.apply(getSharedConnection());
184  }
185
186  /**
187   * Run the column's {@link DbReader} to get the value to return.
188   * See {@link SsComponent#getColumnReader()}.
189   *
190   * @param comp
191   * @return the value read by the DbReader
192   * @throws java.sql.SQLException
193   */
194  static Object runDbReader(SsComponent comp) throws SQLException {
195    // Note that the columnReader implementations typically ignores the
196    // comp argument, but there for special cases.
197    return comp.getColumnReader().apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp);
198  }
199
200  /**
201   * Run the column's {@link DbUpdater} to update the column with the
202   * specified value.
203   * See {@link SsComponent#getColumnUpdater()}.
204   * Throws if nothing written.
205   *
206   * @param comp
207   * @param value
208   * @return actual item written to the database, after possible conversions.
209   * @throws SQLException
210   */
211  static DbUpdate runDbUpdater(SsComponent comp, Object value) throws SQLException {
212    // Note that the columnUpdater implementations typically ignores the
213    // comp argument, but there for special cases.
214    return runDbUpdater(comp, value, comp.getColumnUpdater());
215  }
216
217  /**
218   * For the typical simple cases run the columnUpdater to set the value.
219   * Note that the columnUpdater typically ignores the comp argument, but
220   * there for special cases.
221   *
222   * @param comp
223   * @param value
224   * @param columnUpdater
225   * @return actual item written to the database, throws if nothing written
226   * @throws SQLException
227   */
228  // TODO: any reason to make this public?
229  private static DbUpdate runDbUpdater(
230      SsComponent comp, Object value, DbUpdater<RowSet, Integer, SsComponent, Object> columnUpdater)
231      throws SQLException {
232    return columnUpdater.apply(comp.getRowSet(), comp.getColumnIndex(), comp, value);
233  }
234
235  /**
236   * Like Runnable, but throws.
237   */
238  interface RunnableSQL {
239    /**
240     * @throws SQLException
241     */
242    void run() throws SQLException;
243  }
244
245  /**
246   *
247   * @param <T>
248   */
249  interface ConsumerSQL<T> {
250    /**
251     *
252     * @param t
253     * @throws SQLException
254     */
255    public void accept(T t) throws SQLException;
256  }
257
258  /**
259   * Like Function, but only has apply method that throws SQLException.
260   * @param <T>
261   * @param <R>
262   */
263  interface FunctionSQL<T, R> {
264    /**
265     * Run the function.
266     * @param t
267     * @return
268     * @throws SQLException
269     */
270    public R apply(T t) throws SQLException;
271  }
272
273  /**
274   * Like BiFunction, but throws SQLException.
275   *
276   * @param <T>
277   * @param <U>
278   * @param <R>
279   */
280  interface BiFuncSQL<T, U, R> {
281    /**
282     * Run the function
283     * @param t
284     * @param u
285     * @return
286     * @throws SQLException
287     */
288    public R apply(T t, U u) throws SQLException;
289  }
290
291  /**
292   * Three arg function taking rowSet,colIdx,comp that throws SQLException
293   * and returns an Object.
294   *
295   * @param <T>
296   * @param <U>
297   * @param <V>
298   */
299
300  interface DbReader<T, U, V> {
301    /**
302     * Run the function
303     *
304     * @param t
305     * @param u
306     * @param v
307     * @return value read from database
308     * @throws SQLException
309     */
310
311    public Object apply(T t, U u, V v) throws SQLException;
312  }
313
314  /**
315   * Four arg function taking rowSet,colIdx,comp,value that throws SQLException
316   * and returns an Object.
317   *
318   * @param <T>
319   * @param <U>
320   * @param <V>
321   * @param <W>
322   */
323  interface DbUpdater<T, U, V, W> {
324    /**
325     * Run the function
326     *
327     * @param t
328     * @param u
329     * @param v
330     * @param w
331     * @return The actual item written to the database
332     * @throws SQLException
333     */
334
335    public DbUpdate apply(T t, U u, V v, W w) throws SQLException;
336  }

338  /**
339   * Extracts the inner element type of an array column using meta data.
340   * The result may be vendor specific.
341   * @param metaData
342   * @param columnIndex
343   * @return
344   * @throws SQLException
345   */
346  private static String getVendorTypeNameForArray(ResultSetMetaData metaData, int columnIndex)
347      throws SQLException {
348    String rawTypeName = metaData.getColumnTypeName(columnIndex);
349    if (rawTypeName == null) {
350      return null;
351    }
352
353    // Standardize string layout: uppercase, trimmed, and strip parameterized sizes like (255)
354    String cleanName
355        = rawTypeName.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT).replaceAll("\\(\\d+(?:,\\s*\\d+)?\\)", "").trim();
356
357    // 1. Handle "INTEGER ARRAY" / "VARCHAR ARRAY" formats (H2, HSQLDB, DuckDB)
358    if (cleanName.endsWith(" ARRAY")) {
359      cleanName = cleanName.substring(0, cleanName.indexOf(" ARRAY")).trim();
360    }
361
362    // 2. Handle standard suffix arrays like "varchar[]" or "int4[]"
363    if (cleanName.endsWith("[]")) {
364      cleanName = cleanName.substring(0, cleanName.length() - 2).trim();
365    }
366
367    // 3. Handle PostgreSQL legacy array prefix representation ("_int4", "_text")
368    if (cleanName.startsWith("_")) {
369      cleanName = cleanName.substring(1).trim();
370    }
371
372    // 4. Handle functional notation wrapper syntax like ClickHouse "Array(Int32)"
373    if (cleanName.startsWith("ARRAY(") && cleanName.endsWith(")")) {
374      cleanName = cleanName.substring(6, cleanName.length() - 1).trim();
375    }
376    return cleanName;
377  }
378}
